neighbours.label: The end of a general factual or evaluative claim in expository writing (space travel is expensive., Americans are living longer.), the boundary before the supporting evidence, vs sentence ends in narrative or instructions
fire: Studies show that teenagers are sleeping less than ever. Phones are one reason.
Owning a car in a big city is remarkably costly. Parking alone can exceed rent.
It is clear that coral reefs are shrinking. Surveys from the last decade agree.
Electric bikes have become enormously popular. Sales doubled in three years.
Evidence suggests that people are marrying later. The median age keeps rising.
Housing in coastal towns is increasingly unaffordable; prices rose 40 percent.
Research confirms that bees are declining quickly. Pesticides are a major factor.
Remote work is now widespread among office staff: one in three works from home.
quiet: The teenager put his phone down and turned off the light. He fell asleep.
She parked the car in the garage and carried the bags inside. It was raining.
We swam out to the coral reef and back. Then we ate lunch on the boat.
He bought an electric bike on Saturday. He rode it to his aunt's house.
Chop the onions finely. Add them to the pan with a little oil.
They walked along the coast until sunset; then they found a small inn.
The bee landed on the rose and stayed there. My daughter watched it closely.
Turn left at the bank and walk two blocks: the office is on your right.

predictions: The final word or punctuation of a general claim in explanatory prose reaches 0.2-0.5; sentence ends in stories, recipes and greetings stay under 0.05.
short: end of an expository claim before evidence
notes: Card: 15 of 32 peaks on '.', then ';', ',', ' --', ':' closing a general claim in journalism ('is undeniable.', 'living longer.', 'historically low;').
